usage_rule: Structured input ONLY. Never paste these patterns or their examples as prose into a prompt or a critic's window: prompt text demonstrating a form teaches it and scores as it (prompt-text-poisons-its-own-detector; the 305 gate's re-ask carries no rule text for the same reason). Consumers cite this file by path+version; a new version is a new file line, never an in-place semantic change.

banned_words.treatment: delete the label; if the sentence needs the meaning, show it by being plain

banned_words.owner_words: the word was overused across the estate
banned_words.treatment: delete the label; keep being straight; the one blessed exception is idea.uk's report hero (decision record D-005)

banned_words.name: plain_words
banned_words.authority: owner ruling 2026-09-02 (decision 7: v2 GO), generalising ruling 9
banned_words.treatment: delete the label; a site that must SAY its words are plain is not showing it — same remedy as 'plainly'

banned_shapes.name: x_not_y
banned_shapes.treatment: truncate before the comparison (ruling 7): keep the first half, end the sentence
banned_shapes.note: v2: dash-separated forms added (em/en dash, spaced or unspaced; spaced hyphen) — documentation proxy; negXNotYRe in negationtells.go decides

banned_shapes.name: rather_than
banned_shapes.treatment: as x_not_y; forgiveness level pending owner Q-A
banned_shapes.note: the canary proved the model prior produces this without any demonstration present; only mechanical repair or a different model clears it

banned_shapes.name: instead_of
banned_shapes.treatment: as x_not_y; named by the owner in ruling 7; gate-vocabulary addition pending Q-B

banned_shapes.name: not_just
banned_shapes.treatment: as x_not_y; gate-vocabulary addition pending Q-B

banned_shapes.name: negative_reveal
banned_shapes.treatment: state the positive fact first; fold any earned contrast in afterwards
banned_shapes.note: broad proxy; the gate's own definition is narrower (opening-reveal); read before convicting mid-sentence matches

banned_classes_no_regex.name: internal_directive_explanation
banned_classes_no_regex.owner_words: very much about our internal directives rather than describing what we do in terms that the user will understand might be a benefit to them
banned_classes_no_regex.shape: copy that explains WHY we wrote it the way we wrote it, or narrates our editorial rules as content

banned_classes_no_regex.name: presumption
banned_classes_no_regex.owner_words: we mustn't presume to know what they want or what things actually are useful to them
banned_classes_no_regex.shape: asserting the visitor's intent, situation or need as fact; conditional openings (if/when/where) are the compliant form
banned_classes_no_regex.detection: openers asserting the reader's state; read

banned_classes_no_regex.name: register_labelling
banned_classes_no_regex.shape: any sentence describing the site's own tone, method or virtue as a selling point

changelog: v2 (owner ruling 2026-09-02, decision 7 GO): (1) banned_words gains the plain-words register-labelling collocation family — the 'plainly' cousin flagged in 668's header (mortgagecalculator r6) and ruled in. (2) x_not_y's documentation pattern gains the dash-separated form ('straight guidance at every price point — not a default to premium') found live by the offer lane's gate on garden-tools.uk: comma-anchored patterns missed it in the register, negationtells.go AND the gate's re-scan — a repaired point was recorded clean while carrying it. The Go regex (negXNotYRe) is the authority and widens in the same commit; same shape NAME, per the lockstep's names-only contract.
